questions: When a string contains no commas, does the function return the original string unchanged, or should it still be processed (e.g., split into characters)?
If a string contains multiple consecutive commas (e.g., 'a,,b'), how should the empty substrings between commas be handled? Are they considered elements to be randomized?
Should the randomization be applied per string independently, or should the random seed affect all strings collectively (e.g., using the same random sequence across all strings)?
Are leading/trailing spaces around the entire string preserved in the output, or are they normalized away?
If a substring itself contains a comma (e.g., escaped or within quotes), should it be treated as a delimiter or as part of the element?
Does the function guarantee that the randomized string is different from the original whenever possible (i.e., at least two distinct substrings)?
Should the output DataFrame have a specific index (e.g., default range index) or preserve the original list's indexing?
What should happen if the input list contains non-string items (e.g., numbers, None)? Are they converted to strings or raise an error?
